channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Agri Stats case ready for trial, judge says
item.description: The Department of Justice may proceed with its claims that Agri Stats operated an illegal information exchange to inflate prices for chicken, pig and cow products across the US, a Minnesota federal court has ruled.

item.title: Competition Tribunal denies leave in Canada’s first public interest application
item.description: In the first application since recent amendments to Canada’s Competition Act came into force, Canada’s Competition Tribunal declined to grant leave to a private applicant seeking to bring a case against Alphabet, Google and Apple before the tribunal under the new ‘public interest’ test. This highly anticipated decision marks the tribunal’s first opportunity to provide guidance on the application o...

item.title: Bill to pay: The Briefing for 25 February 2026
item.description: The EU’s General Court today told Skadden Arps Slate Meagher & Flom partner Bill Batchelor to pay legal costs after he unsuccessfully challenged the European Commission's refusal to disclose documents about the designation of his client ByteDance under the Digital Markets Act. Also in The Briefing, Microsoft is raided in Japan, and a €7 billion antitrust damages claim against Google gets a jud...

item.title: Divestments not enough in EU Google adtech case, complainant warns
item.description: Forcing Google to sell off key elements of its advertising technology infrastructure will not “solve the monopoly problem” that allows the tech company to “control” the sector, a lead complainant has told the European Commission.

item.title: BRG poaches telecoms expert from Frontier Economics
item.description: Berkeley Research Group has hired Martin Duckworth from Frontier Economics as a managing director in London.

item.title: Ryanair kicks off fight against Italian abuse penalty
item.description: Ryanair has appealed against a €255 million Italian abuse of dominance fine, sticking to defences it raised last year against the national antitrust watchdog’s statement of objections.

item.title: MEP questions EU’s ability to tackle serial acquisitions
item.description: The European Commission’s response to concerns about Remondis’ alleged “serial acquisition strategy” in the waste management sector signals the agency may not have the tools to address creeping market concentration, a European lawmaker has claimed.

item.title: Judge: Live Nation trial going ahead
item.description: A Manhattan federal judge has signalled he would reject Live Nation’s request to pause the Department of Justice’s monopolisation suit to allow for an immediate appeal against the case’s survival.

item.title: Axinn poaches trio from US agencies
item.description: Former Federal Trade Commission attorney Daniel Matheson and Department of Justice lawyers Katrina Rouse and Jimmy Moore have joined the partnership at Axinn Veltrop & Harkrider.

item.title: Man on the inside: The Tipline for 25 February 2026
item.description: The list of opponents to the Netflix/Warner Bros merger grows longer as 11 Republican state attorneys general tell the Department of Justice they are concerned the tie-up would harm consumers and theatres. Netflix chief executive Ted Sarandos is reportedly visiting the White House tomorrow to discuss the proposal just days after President Trump demanded the resignation of one of its board members....
